average.title: Averaging neighbors removes the whine
average.caption: Each output is the average of a sample and the one before it. The whine’s neighbors cancel to 0; the slow 500 Hz tone barely changes.

wheel.title: Every tone turns a wheel
wheel.caption: A tone is a dot turning 360° × tone ÷ 8,000 per sample. Its left-right position at each stop is the sample.

midpoint.title: The average is a midpoint
midpoint.caption: Zoomed in on the rim: the average of two dots is the midpoint of the chord between them, 0.98 from the center. The short gap to the rim is the 2% the average loses at 500 Hz.

radians.title: Radians: a turn measured by the walk
radians.caption: Lay the walk along the rim flat on a ruler: a full turn of a radius-1 wheel is 2π, about 6.28.

unit-circle.title: The unit circle: one spot per tone
unit-circle.caption: Every tone gets a fixed spot: where its dot lands after one sample. The angle in radians is ω.

zero.title: The average has one zero
zero.caption: How much of a tone passes is its distance to the zero, compared with 2, the distance of 0 Hz.

j-turn.title: j is a quarter turn
j-turn.caption: Times j turns an arrow a quarter turn counter-clockwise. Two quarter turns make a flip: j × j = −1.

multiply.title: Multiplying points: sizes multiply, angles add
multiply.caption: Dashed arrows go in; the solid arrow is the product. The angles stack end to end while the lengths multiply.

spinning-arrow.title: The tone is a turning arrow
spinning-arrow.caption: The arrow’s left-right shadow is the sample you have read off the wheel since lesson 3. Times j adds 90° to its angle.

delay.title: A delay turns the dot back
delay.caption: The copy one sample old sits ω clockwise behind the fresh dot: multiplying by z⁻¹ turns a point ω clockwise.

mirror-arrow.title: A real tone is two arrows
mirror-arrow.caption: Left: an arrow and its mirror arrow add up to a real tone. Right: a zero on one arrow removes only that half.

dull.title: Zeros at ±j dull 1,500 Hz
dull.caption: Multiply the distances to both zeros, then compare with 0 Hz: 1,500 Hz keeps only 38%.

zero-pair.title: A zero pair at any angle
zero-pair.caption: Put the pair at the whine’s angle θ and its mirror. The middle weight of the program is −2cos θ.

z-plane.title: The size of H over the whole plane
z-plane.caption: A relief map of the size of H, its front edge cut through the zero at j. Tones only walk the rim; the height under a tone is how much of it passes.

feedback.title: Feedback: the filter listens to itself
feedback.caption: The loop on the right is the feedback: each output is fed back, two samples later, times −0.81.

notch.title: A pole beside the zero saves the voice
notch.caption: Up close: far from the notch, a tone’s distances to the zero and the pole nearly cancel. Only close to 2,000 Hz does the zero win.

gain-curves.title: Three filters, three gain curves
gain-curves.caption: The notch removes 2,000 Hz and keeps almost everything else; the two-back filter takes the middle of the voice with it.

echo.title: A pole’s radius: how much an echo keeps
echo.caption: The feedback loop alone, no zeros. Each echo is the last one times −r²; only poles inside the circle let it die out.
